title: What If Every Car on the Road Drove Itself?

scenes.text: What if every car drove itself? Crashes wouldn't vanish. A study says most would stay.
Humans cause about ninety-four percent of U.S. crashes, so people expect self-driving cars to fix almost everything.
The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety studied more than five thousand crashes with causes collected by federal investigators.
Self-driving cars would likely stop the ones caused by distraction, drunk driving and falling asleep.
But they could still misjudge another car's speed, drive too fast for the road, or botch an evasive move.
The result: only about a third of crashes prevented, even if every vehicle were autonomous. Safer roads need smarter driving.

description:
What if every car drove itself?
An IIHS study of more than 5,000 crashes found self-driving cars would prevent only about a third of them.
